nonop.heading: Non-Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Non-interest expense decreased year-over year by $5 million, or 2%, to $296 million. The non-GAAP measure of operating non-interest expense decreased by $8 million, or 3%, to $287 million. This primarily reflected lower operating expenses due to branch sales and consolidations. Non-operating expenses of $9 million in 2024 and $6 million in 2023 included branch and facilities consolidations in both years, and 2024 expenses related to the pending merger.

The largest decrease in operating expense was occupancy and equipment expense, which decreased $4 million or 12%. This included the impact of four branch consolidations in 2023, three branch consolidations in 2024, and ten branches sold in 2024, together with dispositions of other excess properties. Of note, the sales of eight of the branches sold were completed near the end of the third quarter of 2024. All major categories of operating expenses declined year-over-year except for regulatory expense and compensation expense. The Company is focused on efficiencies to reduce overhead and to deepen its investment in frontline staff and customer engagement technology. Full year compensation expense increased 1% year-over-year. Fourth quarter compensation expense decreased 3% year-over-year. Year-end full time equivalent staff totaled 1,216 positions in 2024, a decrease of 124 positions, or 9%, from 1,340 positions at year-end 2023.

net.text: Berkshire reported 2024 net income of $61 million, or $1.43 per share, compared to $70 million, or $1.60 per share, in 2023. The decrease in 2024 was due primarily to higher non-operating losses on the sale of securities.

net.text: Summary. First quarter results were net income of $26 million in 2025 compared to a net loss of $20 million in 2024. Results in 2024 include a $50 million non-operating loss on the sale of securities. First quarter operating income increased year-over-year by $7 million, or 32%, to $28 million reflecting a $5 million increase in operating revenue and a $4 million decrease in operating expenses. Operating revenue increased due to a $2 million increase in net interest income and a $3 million increase in operating non-interest income. The efficiency ratio improved year-over-year to 59.5% from 66.3%, achieving the most favorable quarterly level in two years.

prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provisions for credit losses are set forth below:

(1) Includes Merger Day 1 unfunded credit commitment totaling $8.4 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the provision for credit losses decreased $11.4 million to $8.9 million, compared to a provision for credit losses of $20.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in the provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 is primarily driven by a release in the provision for unfunded commitments.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, the provision for credit and investment losses was $21.8 million and $33.3 million, respectively.

See management’s discussion of “Financial Condition — Allowance for Loan and Lease Losses” and Note 5, “Allowance for Credit Losses,” to the unaudited consolidated financial statements for a description of how management determined the allowance for loan and lease losses for each portfolio and class of loans.

nonint.text:
The following table sets forth the components of non-interest expense:

Merger and restructuring expense decreased $40.8 million, to $5.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $45.9 million for the same period in 2025, and decreased $29.1 million, to $18.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $47.3 million for the same period in 2025. Excluding merger and restructuring expense, non-interest expense increased $44.2 million to $127.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $83.4 million for the same period in 2025, and increased $182.5 million to $382.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $200.1 million for the same period in 2025, primarily driven by activity due to the Transaction.

Compensation and employee benefits expense increased $19.4 million, or 38.9%, to $69.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $50.0 million for the same period in 2025, and increased $88.4 million, or 73.0%, to $209.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $121.0 million for the same period in 2025, primarily driven by activity due to the Transaction.

Equipment and data processing expense increased $5.9 million, or 53.0%, to $17.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $11.1 million for the same period in 2025,…

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text:
The Company recorded an income tax expense of $20.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to an income tax benefit of $4.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing effective tax rates of 25.0% and 49.8%, respectively. The decrease in the effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily driven by income tax benefits having a proportionally smaller impact relative to the level of pre-tax income in 2026 as compared to the level of pre-tax loss in 2025.

The Company recorded an income tax expense of $62.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to an income tax expense of $9.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing effective tax rates of 26.7% and 20.9%, respectively. The increase in the effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily driven by higher pre-tax income and Transaction related items, including the discrete tax impact of nondeductible expenses.

net.heading: Net Income (Loss)
net.text:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $61.2 million, or $0.73 per basic and diluted share, an increase of $65.4 million, from a net loss of $(4.2) million, or $(0.05) per basic and diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This increase in net income is primarily the result of an increase in net interest income of $68.3 million, an increase in non-interest income of $13.7 million, and a decrease in provision for credit losses on loans of $11.4 million, partially offset by an increase in the provision for income taxes of $24.5 million and an increase of $3.4 million in non-interest expense. The net loss for three months ended September 30, 2025 was driven by one-time costs of $54.3 million, pre-tax, due to the Merger. Refer to " Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Reconciliation to GAAP" for operating earnings measures. Refer to “Results of Operations" below for further discussion.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $171.8 million, or $2.05 per basic and diluted share, an increase of $134.9 million, from $36.9 million, or $0.42 per basic share and $0.41 per diluted share for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income increased $68.3 million to $197.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $128.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This increase reflects a $75.8 million increase in interest income on loans and leases, along with a $10.7 million increase in interest income in investment securities, partially offset by a $18.2 million increase in interest expense on deposits and borrowings. The increases year over year are primarily a result of the Transaction. Refer to “Results of Operations - Comparison of the Three-Month Period Ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025 — Interest Income” and “Results of Operations - Comparison of the Three-Month Period Ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025 — Interest Expense - Deposit and Borrowed Funds” below for more details.

Net interest income increased $277.8 million to $581.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $303.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase reflects a $321.1 million increase in interest income on loans and leases, along with a $43.7 million increase in interest income in investment securities, partially offset by a $87.0 million increase in interest expense on deposits and borrowings. The increases year over year are primarily a result of the Transaction.

intro.text: Beacon Financial Corporation, a Delaware corporation, is the holding company for Beacon Bank & Trust and its subsidiaries and Clarendon Private. The Company offers a wide range of commercial, business and retail banking services, including a full complement of cash management products, foreign exchange services, on-line and mobile banking services, consumer and residential loans and wealth management services. Clarendon Private is a registered investment advisor with the SEC. Through Clarendon Private and the Trust and Investments Division of the Bank, the Company offers a wide range of wealth management services to individuals, families, endowments and foundations to help these clients meet their long-term financial goals.

accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: Loan-to-value ratios depend on the collateral type and generally do not exceed 80 percent of orderly liquidation value or net book value as reported on the borrower’s financial statements.
This team is the Bank’s largest source of commercial lending fee revenue.
Management primarily relies on internal risk management staff to review the risk ratings of the majority of commercial loan balances.
Deposits are the major source of funds for the Bank’s lending and investment activities.
The Company relies on and continues to recruit employees with the right mix of skills, expertise and experiences.

Real estate market conditions affect the value and marketability of real estate collateral, and they also affect the cash flows, liquidity, and net worth of many borrowers whose operations and finances depend on real estate market conditions.

The Company emphasizes commercial lending, which generally exposes the Company to a greater risk of nonpayment and loss because repayment of such loans often depends on the successful operations and income stream of the borrowers.

The extent to which an Event impacts our business, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations will depend on future developments, which are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted, including the scope and duration of an Event, the continued effectiveness of our business continuity plan, the direct and indirect impact of an Event on our customers, colleagues, counterparties and service providers, and actions taken by governmental authorities and other third parties in response to an Event.
The Company relies on industry standard internet security and authentication systems to effect secure transmission of data.
The Company also utilizes services from major vendors of technology, telecommunications, and other essential operating services.

The benefits of this strategy will depend on our ability to realize expected benefits without experiencing significant customer attrition, unexpected costs, or unanticipated disruptions to operations.
Net interest income is the Company's largest source of income.
The Company relies on its ability to generate deposits and effectively manage the repayment of its liabilities to ensure that there is adequate liquidity to fund operations.

Other primary sources of funds consist of cash flows from operations, maturities and sales of investment securities and/or loans, brokered deposits, borrowings from the FHLB and/or and the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston discount window, and unsecured borrowings.
The Company's ability to raise capital, if needed, will depend on its condition and performance, and on market conditions.
The level of interest and trading in the Company’s stock depends on many factors beyond the Company's control.
Analysts also rely on these measures in estimating and evaluating the Company’s performance.
This measure primarily relies on the measures of operating revenue and operating expense already used in the Company’s calculation of its efficiency ratio.
The primary sources of funds were securities sales, together with operating activities and the stock issuance.
